chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Yunis, from Abi Hamzah, from one of the Imams (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was informed that a person had been killed in the mosque of Juhaynah. The Messenger of Allah rose and walked until he reached their mosque. He said: 'The people heard and came to him. He asked: Who killed this man?' They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we do not know who killed him.'

He said: 'A Muslim who is killed, whose killers are unknown, by Allah who sent me with the truth, if the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth shared in the blood of a Muslim or were pleased with it, Allah would throw them on their beaks into the Fire,' or he said: 'on their faces.'

key_terms.أَهْلَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ: The inhabitants of the heavens and the earth
key_terms.قَتِیلٌ: A killed person, specifically one whose killer is unknown
key_terms.مَسْجِدُ جُهَیْنَةَ: The mosque of the Juhaynah tribe
key_terms.مَنَاخِرِهِمْ: Their beaks (a metaphor for prostration or being cast down)
key_terms.مَنْ ظَهَرَ إِلَيْهِ: Whom it became apparent to / whose responsibility it was

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence for the heavens and earth if a Muslim is killed and the killer is unknown?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal* highlights the gravity of *Damm al-Mu'min* (blood of a Muslim) in cases of *Qatl al-Majhul* (unknown killer), emphasizing collective responsibility. The Prophet’s declaration that Allah would cast the inhabitants of the heavens and earth into Hellfire if they shared in or were pleased with such blood underscores the cosmic significance of a single Muslim's life. This narrative is frequently cited in Shia jurisprudence to illustrate the severity of communal complicity in unresolved murders.
